newsitem.title: USA: KKK may sue Pittsburgh for right to rally.
newsitem.headline: KKK may sue Pittsburgh for right to rally.

text.p: The Ku Klux Klan will file a federal lawsuit against the city of Pittsburgh if the mayor does not reverse his decision to ban the white supremacist group from holding a rally, the KKK's attorney said Wednesday.

"I'll give (Mayor Tom Murphy) time to change his mind," said Robert Wiggins, a civil lawyer in Detroit who represents the KKK nationally. "We'll be filing a federal lawsuit if he doesn't ... making him give my guys their first and fourteenth amendment rights."
Wiggins said a suit could be filed within a week. Murphy Tuesday rejected a request by the KKK for a permit to hold a rally in Pittsburgh April 5, saying it could provoke violence.
City officials and klan members were not available for comment Wednesday.

The KKK has gone to court in other cities where they were banned to try to win permission to rally. "(The KKK) has a constitutional right to assemble, they have a freedom of speech right," Wiggins said.
